c-sm-compare.label: Comparing and ordering fractions
c-sm-compare.summary: Put fractions against a common yardstick (a decimal, or a benchmark like 0.6) instead of finding a common denominator.

c-sm-bodmas.label: BODMAS with nested fractions
c-sm-bodmas.summary: Work from the innermost bracket outwards, keep fractions exact, and estimate first so options can be struck.

q-sm-order.label: Arrange fractions in order
q-sm-order.summary: Four fractions to put in ascending or descending order.

q-sm-bodmas.label: Evaluate nested brackets and mixed numbers
q-sm-bodmas.summary: Brackets inside brackets, mixed numbers and a division; or a very plain sum with decimals.

q-sm-decimal.label: Decimal fractions: cancel before you multiply
q-sm-decimal.summary: Products and quotients of decimals, or a series of decimal fractions that all reduce to the same value.

q-sm-roots.label: Square roots of decimal numbers
q-sm-roots.summary: Sums of √0.49, √59.29 … and statements to be judged true or false.

q-sm-harmonic.label: Series of fractions with a known partial sum
q-sm-harmonic.summary: A series like 5/6 + 5/9 + 5/12 + … written in terms of 1 + 1/2 + 1/3 + … = k.

q-sm-root-trick.label: Expression under a root that is a perfect square
q-sm-root-trick.summary: N = a² − a − (a − 1) and √N asked: rewrite as (a − 1)².

formulas.text: a/b < c/d  ⇔  a×d < c×b   (cross-multiply, b and d positive)
formulas.note: Or compare each fraction with a benchmark such as 1/2 or 0.6.

formulas.text: Closer to 1 means a smaller gap: a/b = 1 − (b − a)/b
Order: Brackets (innermost first), Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction

formulas.text: Cancel before multiplying: (a × b) ÷ (c × d) → pair numerator and denominator factors that share a factor.
formulas.note: Decimals: shift the point the same number of places in numerator and denominator.

formulas.text: √0.49 = 0.7, √0.0049 = 0.07, √59.29 = 7.7: the root has half as many decimal places.
formulas.note: Take the root of the digits, then place the point.

q-sm-order.cue: 'Arrange the fractions … in ascending / descending order.'
q-sm-order.standard: Convert each to a decimal (5/9 = 0.556, 4/7 = 0.571, 3/5 = 0.6, 7/11 = 0.636) and sort.
q-sm-order.fast: Pick a benchmark like 3/5 = 0.6 and sort the others into 'below' and 'above' (cross-multiply once each).
q-sm-order.eliminate: Look at the first and last item of each option. 3/5 is bigger than 5/9 and 4/7, so it cannot be first. That alone removes two options.

q-sm-bodmas.cue: A long expression with brackets inside brackets, mixed numbers and ÷, or a short one with decimals.
q-sm-bodmas.fast: Estimate while you work: 8.33 − (0.78 ÷ 0.18) ≈ 8.33 − 4.4 ≈ 3.9. Only 95/24 ≈ 3.96 is near.
q-sm-bodmas.eliminate: Estimate the whole expression to one decimal; options with the wrong sign or size go at once (−41/15 is negative, 32/3 is above 10).
traps: Doing the division before the bracket.
Adding instead of subtracting inside the middle bracket.

q-sm-continued.cue: A fraction whose denominator contains another fraction, stacked.
q-sm-continued.eliminate: The value is a little above 3 (3 + a fraction less than 1/2). Options above 3.5 or below 3 are out.
traps: Adding 1/3 to 5 and forgetting to flip before adding 2.

q-sm-decimal.cue: Several decimals multiplied and divided, or a row of decimal fractions that look the same.
q-sm-decimal.standard: Remove the decimals (multiply top and bottom by the same power of 10) and cancel before you multiply.
q-sm-decimal.fast: A row of fractions where numerator and denominator shrink together: every term has the same value; multiply by the count.
q-sm-decimal.eliminate: Estimate each part to one significant figure; options far from that are out.
traps: Misplacing the decimal point after multiplying.
Adding the terms as if they differed.

q-sm-roots.cue: A true/false statement with several square roots of decimals.
q-sm-roots.standard: Take each root exactly (0.49 → 0.7, 0.0049 → 0.07, 59.29 → 7.7) and add; compare with the right side.
q-sm-roots.fast: Roots of decimals: halve the number of decimal places, then take the integer root.
q-sm-roots.eliminate: Check the last decimal place: the sum of the roots' last digits must match the claimed total.

q-sm-harmonic.cue: A series whose terms are a constant times 1/2, 1/3, 1/4 … and a known sum k.
q-sm-harmonic.standard: Factor out the constant; match the remaining series with the known one and remove any missing first term.
q-sm-harmonic.fast: The first term 1 of 1 + 1/2 + … is not in the new series, so subtract it: k − 1.
q-sm-harmonic.eliminate: Compare sizes: the new sum has no 1 and a 5/3 multiplier.
traps: Forgetting to remove the first term 1.
Using 5/6 as the first term of 5/3 × series: 5/6 is 5/3 × 1/2.

q-sm-root-trick.cue: A big number squared minus consecutive numbers, with a square root asked.
q-sm-root-trick.standard: Let a be the big number and rewrite every other number in terms of a.
q-sm-root-trick.eliminate: √N must be just below the big number, so options near it are the only ones possible.
